hypotheses.statement: The incident was caused by an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which caused TLS handshake failures in the checkout-api payments-connector, leading to 502 errors and high latency on POST /v2/checkout/submit.
The release 2026.5.14-a was not the cause of the incident, as it contained no changes to the POST /v2/checkout/submit code path, and the system recovered before the rollback completed.

observed_facts.statement: Release 2026.5.14-a deployed to production at 09:09:52Z, two minutes and eleven seconds before alert-4471 fired. Changes: copy edits to three checkout confirmation email templates, and a dependency bump of the CSV export library used by the nightly reconciliation job. No code path in this release is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit.

checkout-api payments-connector: repeated outbound TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443. Error: certificate verify failed: certificate has expired. First occurrence 09:11:47Z, sustained at 40-60 events per second.
checkout-api: POST /v2/checkout/submit returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries. Correlated with payments-connector TLS failures.
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired. Observed 5xx ratio 0.184 over a 5 minute window against an objective of 0.005. Affected route: POST /v2/checkout/submit. Alert remained firing until 09:58:10Z.

Alert checkout-api-latency fired. p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose from 240ms to 10400ms. The 10400ms value sits at the configured client timeout, which is a ceiling rather than a measured completion time.
INC-7742 opened at 09:15:00Z, severity 1, title 'Checkout submit failing for all customers'. Impact field left empty. No customer-impact estimate was recorded at any point during the incident.
Responder A: 'We shipped 2026.5.14-a two minutes before this started. That is almost certainly the cause, let us roll it back.'

Trace 5f21c0: POST /v2/checkout/submit total 10402ms. Span checkout.validate 12ms ok. Span payments.authorize 10388ms error, terminated by client timeout, no upstream response recorded. No span entered the email template or CSV export code paths.

Responder B: 'The release only touched email templates and the CSV export dependency. Nothing in it is on the submit path. The connector logs show expired-certificate TLS failures starting at 09:11:47Z, which is before the alert but after the deploy. I think we are looking at the payments gateway certificate.'
checkout-api payments-connector: outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeding again. Error rate returned to baseline at 09:57:55Z.

Responder C from the payments-gateway team: 'Our leaf certificate for payments-gateway.internal expired at 09:11:40Z. We rotated it and it took effect at 09:57:50Z. We have no record of who owns the renewal automation for that host.'
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z. The 5xx ratio had already returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before this rollback completed.
INC-7742 marked resolved. Resolution note reads only 'rolled back and recovered'. The note does not mention the certificate rotation reported in the incident channel.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or runbook identifying the owner of certificate renewal automation for payments-gateway.internal.
open_questions.question: Who is responsible for the certificate renewal automation for payments-gateway.internal?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Quantitative impact assessment (e.g., number of failed transactions, affected customers, revenue impact).
open_questions.question: What was the customer and business impact of the incident?

summary: An expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal caused TLS handshake failures in the checkout-api payments-connector, leading to 502 errors and high latency on the checkout submit endpoint. The incident was initially misattributed to a recent deployment, but recovery occurred before the rollback completed, confirming the certificate as the root cause.

timeline.statement: Payments connector TLS handshake failures begin.
Responder attributes incident to the release.
